rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a concrete, material component of the child: the distinctive description of the National Capital's sesquicentennial as 150 years since establishment of the permanent federal seat in the District of Columbia in 1800, together with an appeal for citizens to participate in the observances. The child adapts that material into an Independence Day proclamation. C13 and C12 have related ceremonial calls and freedom-oriented language, but their overlap is less distinctive and less directly tied to the child's special sesquicentennial recital.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In special recognition of the sesquicentennial year of our National Capital, which marks the progress achieved during the one hundred and fifty years since the establishment of the permanent seat of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia in the year 1800
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the commemoration of the one hundred and fiftieth anniversary of the establishment of the permanent seat of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia in the year 1800
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, substantially shared factual language, lightly recast to emphasize progress.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do urge all our citizens to participate in appropriate ceremonies and celebrations
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby invite American citizens from every region of our country to come to their Nation's Capital and participate in the sesquicentennial observances
shared_material.explanation: Both use a presidential appeal for citizens to participate in the same sesquicentennial commemoration, with the child adapting it to combined Independence Day observances.
